title: L'inspectrice des impôts arrive  (The Tax Inspector Arrives)

segments.t: Earlier today Andréa promised her ex-boyfriend Clément a luxury suite at Cannes if he replaced Colette within a week. Yet the moment Andréa meets Colette face to face, she has the strange feeling they have met before, and decides she can handle her after all. Listen to the French first, without worrying about catching every single word.
Andréa. Voici la dame du centre des impôts.
Bonjour. Andréa Martel.
Colette Brancillon. J'ai besoin d'un bureau pour travailler.
Notre patron est mort il y a trois semaines.
J'ai vraiment l'impression de vous connaître.
Non, je ne crois pas.
C'était peut-être dans une autre vie.
Vous avez tout ce qu'il vous faut?
Oui, merci.
Mon bureau est juste là. À tout à l'heure.
D'accord, merci.
Salut, Clément, c'est Andréa.
Avec Colette Brancillon, ça va aller. On oublie notre accord.
Elle va rester ici pendant des semaines?
Et on peut faire faillite?
Oui. Mais c'est la vie.
Let's walk through it together. After checking that the inspector doesn't mind Arlette's dog, Gabriel brings her to Andréa.
Andréa. Voici la dame du centre des impôts.
'Andréa. Here is the lady from the tax office.' Literally 'the centre of the taxes'. The first word is how you present someone who has just arrived.
Bonjour. Andréa Martel.
'Hello. Andréa Martel.' People often introduce themselves simply by saying hello and giving their full name.
Colette Brancillon. J'ai besoin d'un bureau pour travailler.
'Colette Brancillon. I need an office to work in.' Literally 'I have need of an office for to work'. Colette gets straight down to business.
Notre patron est mort il y a trois semaines.
'Our boss died three weeks ago.' The little three-word phrase before 'three weeks' means 'ago' when it comes before a length of time. Andréa is apologising for the mess at the agency.
J'ai vraiment l'impression de vous connaître.
'I really have the feeling I know you.' In French you say 'the impression of knowing you', using the verb for knowing a person. Andréa stares at Colette, sure she has seen her face somewhere.
Non, je ne crois pas.
'No, I don't think so.' Literally 'I do not believe'. Colette's answer is cool and polite, using the two-part negative around the verb.
C'était peut-être dans une autre vie.
'Maybe it was in another life.' The verb at the front is the past form for how things were, and the hyphenated word after it means 'maybe'.
Vous avez tout ce qu'il vous faut?
'Do you have everything you need?' Literally 'all that which it you is-needed'. A polite, standard phrase when showing a visitor to a room.
Oui, merci.
'Yes, thank you.' Short and polite. Colette doesn't waste a syllable.
Mon bureau est juste là.
'My office is right there.' The word for 'my' is masculine here to match 'office'.
À tout à l'heure.
'See you later.' You use this when you will see the person again later the same day.
D'accord, merci.
'Okay, thank you.' Now Colette shuts the door, and Andréa immediately phones Clément to cancel her expensive Cannes bribe.
Salut, Clément, c'est Andréa.
'Hi, Clément, it's Andréa.' On the phone, French speakers introduce themselves with 'it is' plus their name.
Avec Colette Brancillon, ça va aller.
'With Colette Brancillon, it'll be fine.' Literally 'it is going to go'. Andréa thinks she can charm the young inspector.
On oublie notre accord.
'Forget our deal.' Literally 'we forget our agreement', using the everyday word for 'we'.
Elle va rester ici pendant des semaines?
'Is she going to stay here for weeks?' The verb 'to go' plus 'stay' builds the near future, and the linking word before 'weeks' means 'for' or 'during'.
Et on peut faire faillite?
'And could we go bankrupt?' Literally 'make bankruptcy'. Gabriel is terrified for the agency.
Oui. Mais c'est la vie.
'Yes. But that's life.' Literally 'it is the life'. Andréa shrugs it off, not yet knowing where she really met Colette. Now listen to the whole scene again from start to finish.
Andréa. Voici la dame du centre des impôts.
Bonjour. Andréa Martel.
Colette Brancillon. J'ai besoin d'un bureau pour travailler.
Notre patron est mort il y a trois semaines.
J'ai vraiment l'impression de vous connaître.
Non, je ne crois pas.
C'était peut-être dans une autre vie.
Vous avez tout ce qu'il vous faut?
Oui, merci.
Mon bureau est juste là. À tout à l'heure.
D'accord, merci.
Salut, Clément, c'est Andréa.
Avec Colette Brancillon, ça va aller. On oublie notre accord.
Elle va rester ici pendant des semaines?
Et on peut faire faillite?
Oui. Mais c'est la vie.
Colette is installed in her office, and Andréa has just thrown away her only safety net at the tax office. See you next time!
Bonne soirée!
